inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

facts.text: The README titles the project Deep Reinforcement Learning by Imitation with MuJoCo and Stable Baselines 3
The README says the repository implements DeepMimic and learns controllers for walking robots simulated with the MuJoCo physics engine

The documentation says the environment's step runs the simulation for the configured number of frames and that the MuJoCo simulation runs at 1 kHz, with the policy control frequency equal to the simulation frequency divided by the frame skip
MimicEnv subclasses gym's MujocoEnv and gym.utils.EzPickle
MimicEnv reads the control frequency from the configuration, computes the frame skip from it and initializes MujocoEnv with the MJCF path and that frame skip
MimicEnv.step(action) rescales the action before applying it to the simulation
The upstream step applies the same action for the configured frame skip with do_simulation and, on a MuJoCo exception, resets the environment and ends the episode
The upstream step ends the episode when the COM z position is below 0.5 or the episode reaches the configured maximum length, and returns the old gym four-tuple (observation, reward, done, info)
The alive bonus is 0.2 and the maximum episode duration is 3000 control steps
The default environment id is StraightMimicWalker with a control frequency of 200 Hz
The configured simulation frequency of StraightMimicWalker is 1000 Hz
_rescale_actions clips the policy action to [-1, 1] and scales each element by the action space's high or low value; the comment calls those the joint torque ranges specified in the MJCF file
The observation concatenates the phase variable, the desired walking speed, the joint positions without COM x and the joint velocities
The upstream reset_model takes the initial qpos and qvel from the reference trajectories and applies them to the simulation
The upstream reset lowers the COM z position by the lowest foot corner so that the walker starts in ground contact
MimicWalker3dEnv is the main 3D bipedal walker environment and loads drloco/mujoco/xml/walker3d_flat_feet.xml
MimicWalker165cm65kgEnv loads drloco/mujoco/xml/walker_165cm_65kg.xml
The MJCF root element is <mujoco model="walker3d"> and its compiler element declares angle radian, coordinate local and inertiafromgeom false
The default class gives every motor ctrllimited true, ctrlrange -300 300, gear 1, forcelimited true and forcerange -300 300
The option element selects the RK4 integrator with timestep 0.001 s
The torso body is at 0 0 1.08 and its inertial element gives mass 53.5
The torso carries three slide joints (com_x, com_y, com_z) and three hinge joints (trunk_rot_x, trunk_rot_y, trunk_rot_z); com_z has joint position 0 0 -1.08 and ref 1.08

The right leg has a sagittal hip joint with range -0.8727 0.8727 rad, a frontal hip joint with range -0.7854 0.0873 rad, a knee joint with range 0 2.6180 rad and an ankle joint with range -0.3491 0.6981 rad

The left leg has a sagittal hip joint with range -0.8727 0.8727 rad, a frontal hip joint with range -0.0873 0.7854 rad, a knee joint with range 0 2.6180 rad and an ankle joint with range -0.3491 0.6981 rad
The actuator section declares one motor actuator for each of the eight actuated leg joints

determinism.notes: The stand-in is deterministic from its reset state, but it takes no seed and its placeholder motion is not MuJoCo's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the pinned MJCF for the joint dimensions, the actuator targets and the default motor ctrlrange, but integrates a placeholder motion of each actuated joint
the stand-in loads no geom, contact, constraint, inertia, damping, actuator force or sensor; it ignores the model's mass and joint-range data, so it is not the model's dynamics
the fake has no mj_getState/mj_setState/mj_stateSize, so the bridge uses its basic checkpoint profile: time, qpos, qvel, act and ctrl are restored, not MuJoCo's full integration state
the fake reports the model's own 0.001 s option timestep (drloco/mujoco/xml/walker3d_flat_feet.xml:11) but its per-step motion is placeholder data, not a physical integration
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so the stand-in was not compared with the real engine and the sim backend that imports mujoco was not run

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state and stored ctrl are kept and stay readable. Safety reset advances no ticks and does not clear ctrl; a later explicit step without an action reuses it
